newsitem.title: UK: Moody's may cut English China CP rating.
newsitem.headline: Moody's may cut English China CP rating.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday it placed under review for possible downgrade the prime-1 short term commercial paper rating of English China Clays Plc and the A2 rating of English China Clays Delaware Inc's 7.375 percent notes due 2002 guaranteed by English China Clays Plc.

"The review is based on Moody's concerns about the lack of diversification in English China Clays' earnings which may leave the company more exposed to future cyclical swings in its core paper minerals business," Moody's said in a statement.
"In addition, recent poor trading conditions have led to profit and margin deterioration, asset write-downs and increased debt," it said.

Moody's will assess English China Clays' potential to improve returns from its investment in specialty chemicals, acquired in 1993 to leverage the company's technological expertise in specialty minerals, which continues to perform below management's expectations, it said.

"The review will also consider the possible negative impact on the company's margins and its revenue growth potential from the shift in demand for paper minerals towards calcium carbonates where English China Clays' market position is weaker and its margins are lower than in kaolin, its main paper minerals product," it said.

Moody's said management is conducting a full strategic review of the company and has intensified its cost cutting efforts. Against this background, Moody's review will focus on the company's potential to improve debt protection through its economic cycle.

English China Clays, a world-wide operating producer of paper minerals and specialty chemicals, is the world's largest kaolin producer. It is based in Reading, England. English China Clays Delaware Inc. is its wholly owned subsidiary.
